display.purpose: Page-level title — post hero, home hero. Largest type on screen. Verde profundo in light, cream in dark.

headline.purpose: Major in-post sections. Most-used heading by volume.

body.purpose: Paragraph copy. Raleway 400 at 15px with 1.7 line-height for long-form reading.

label.purpose: The signature treatment for a.text-accent (categories). Uppercase + 600 + 0.08em letter-spacing. Compensates the muted bronze hex with editorial weight so categories pass WCAG AA Normal on cream without losing brand presence.

shadows.name: card-lift
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system. Applied on .card:not(.featured-post):hover. Subtle on cream, visible enough on Forest Floor. Featured cards stay flat (parent .splide__track has overflow:hidden that would chop the shadow).

motion.name: fast
motion.purpose: Tag pill bg/color transition, editorial label color transition.

motion.name: default
motion.purpose: Card hover lift transform + shadow transition.

motion.name: standard
motion.purpose: Button state, generic link hover, form control focus.

motion.name: modal
motion.purpose: Cookie banner enter/exit (opacity + transform + delayed visibility).

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The CTA. Solid British Racing Green bg, white text, theme-aware border. Used for 'Read More', Ko-fi support, Subscribe.

components.name: Outline Primary Button
components.description: Secondary CTA. Transparent at rest, fills with British Racing Green + white text on hover. Used where solid would be too loud.

components.name: Tag Pill
components.description: Ghost-style metadata pill. Uses --eb-tag-* tokens which are theme-aware (translucent verde with verde-darker text in light, translucent lighter-green with bright-green text in dark). Same tokens drive the sidebar tag widget AND footer social icons.
components.css: .ds-tag { display: inline-block; background: var(--eb-tag-bg, rgba(0, 66, 37, 0.10)); color: var(--eb-tag-fg, #002E19); border: 1px solid var(--eb-tag-border, rgba(0, 66, 37, 0.30)); border-radius: 0; padding: 0.5rem 0.85rem; font-family: 'Raleway', sans-serif; font-size: 0.9rem; font-weight: 500; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 0.15s ease, opacity 0.15s ease; } .ds-tag:hover, .ds-tag:focus-visible { background: rgba(var(--bs-primary-rgb, 0, 66, 37), 0.20); color: var(--eb-tag-fg, #002E19); outline: 0; }

components.name: Form Control
components.description: Square 50px-tall input. Body-bg background, cream-green border. Focus shifts border to verde with no glow. Theme-aware via --eb-* tokens.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; height: 50px; background: var(--eb-body-bg, #F2EFE3); color: var(--eb-text-muted, #3D4A40); border: 1px solid var(--eb-border, #C9CDB5); border-radius: 0; padding: 0 12px; font-family: 'Raleway', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; transition: border-color 0.2s ease; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--eb-text-light, #8A9088); font-size: 13px; } .ds-input:focus, .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: var(--bs-primary, #004225); outline: 0; box-shadow: none; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Square surface-shaded container with one-step tonal lift from body. Hover adds the system's only shadow (card-lift). Featured cards on the home slider stay flat at all states. Cover slot uses a literal placeholder gradient — real images would come from Hugo's render-image hook with a srcset.

components.name: Editorial Category Label
components.description: The signature. Uppercase + 600 + 0.08em letter-spacing renders 'ENGINEERING' as a magazine category badge rather than a link. Same pattern used by Vercel, Linear, Stripe, NYT, FT. The trick that lets bronze --bs-accent pass WCAG AA Normal on cream without losing brand presence.
components.css: .ds-category-label-standalone { color: var(--bs-accent, #856814); font-family: 'Raleway', sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; text-decoration: none; transition: color 0.15s ease; } .ds-category-label-standalone:hover, .ds-category-label-standalone:focus-visible { color: var(--bs-accent-darker, #5C440D); outline: 0; }

components.name: Editorial Pagination
components.description: Numbered-text pagination with no boxes. Active page anchored with a 2px ocre underline + font-weight: 600 (the same ocre that marks categories — repeats the accent in two surfaces to unify 'current context'). Arrows muted to text-light. Same pattern as Substack, Stripe Blog, Vercel Blog, NYT. Reserves the underline space at rest to prevent layout shift on hover.

components.name: Code Block
components.description: Block and inline code surfaces. Both use --eb-surface (one tonal step above body) with the border + square corners common to every native surface. Class names mimic Chroma's class-based output (k=keyword, s=string, c=comment, n=name) so the visual matches what the rendered site produces with the manni (light) / dracula (dark) Chroma styles.

narrative.overview:
The name is the system. A notebook in British Racing Green (#004225) — not metaphor, not mood-board — the actual color, treated as identity. Verde profundo headings (#002E19), nugget ocre accents (#856814 light / #C59922 dark), and a warm cream #F2EFE3 body that reads as paper, not screen. Dark mode is a green-tinted forest (#0A1814) — the same notebook, lit from the other side.

The whole point is to not look like the dev-blog category. The verde + ocre + cream was chosen because Giuliano Pertile likes them. Some readers will love it. Some will reject it. Both responses are evidence that the system has identity. A blog no one reacts to is a blog no one remembers.

Density is restrained. Type is set on a warm field. Layout breathes. Motion exists but stays quiet. Shape is uniformly border-radius: 0 — the all-square rule. Every visual decision is documented with its rationale in docs/THEME.md.
keyCharacteristics: British Racing Green is the brand, not a 'primary accent' — heading color, link color, button color, focus ring

Nugget ocre is dual-role with verde, not subordinate — ocre owns the metadata surface (categories, dates, decorative lines), verde owns the action surface (links, buttons, focus, headings). Co-equal in role-distinctness, not in surface coverage: verde dominates by area (≈65%), ocre is rarer by design (≈10%)
The all-square rule: border-radius: 0 on every native surface
Conservatory cream, not white — body bg #F2EFE3 (warm, papered) in light, #0A1814 (green-tinted dark, not black) in dark
Categories are labels, not links — uppercase + 600 + 0.08em letter-spacing
WCAG AA Normal everywhere, AAA on body — light and dark are first-class
Asymmetric ramps — both verde and ocre use different hexes per theme because a token is a role, not a hex constant

rules.name: The Verde-and-Ocre Rule
rules.body: Verde carries action (links, buttons, focus, headings). Ocre carries metadata (categories, dates, decorative lines). The two are co-equal in role-distinctness, NOT in surface coverage — verde dominates by area (≈65% of colored elements), ocre is rarer (≈10%). What matters is that each owns its role exclusively: don't promote ocre to action use; don't demote verde to decoration. The role split is the identity; the area split is just how the roles land in practice.

rules.name: The Tinted-Neutral Rule
rules.body: No pure black (#000), no pure white (#fff) on body surfaces. The only acceptable use of #FFFFFF is text on --eb-brand-solid (.btn-primary, dropdown active), where solid-green-with-white-text is the AAA-passing CTA pattern. Everywhere else: warmth.

rules.name: The Asymmetric-Ramp Rule
rules.body: A token is a role, not a hex constant. Both --bs-primary and --bs-accent resolve to different hexes per theme because the same hex can't carry equal weight on opposite substrates. The Brand-Solid-vs-Brand-Text split (--bs-primary varies, --eb-brand-solid is constant #004225) is the canonical example of this rule applied to a single color family.

rules.name: The Editorial Label Rule
rules.body: Every a.text-accent (categories on cards, post headers, sidebar widget) is rendered as a label, not a link: text-transform: uppercase + font-weight: 600 + letter-spacing: 0.08em + font-size: 0.875rem. The brain reads ENGINEERING as a category badge before parsing the letters. This is the trick that lets bronze #856814 pass WCAG AA Normal on cream — typography carries the brand emphasis the muted hex can't.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Raleway carries everything. Don't add a serif 'for editorial feel'. Don't add a mono 'for code in copy'. The discipline of one family is the editorial choice.

rules.name: The 700-on-Headings Rule
rules.body: Every <h1>-<h6> is Raleway 700. Hierarchy comes from size, not weight contrast. Don't introduce a 500 or 800 headline weight.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows are a response to state — and only one state (hover) on one surface (.card:not(.featured-post)). Don't add ambient shadows to convey 'this is a card'. The tonal step does that.

rules.name: The Tonal-Step Rule
rules.body: When you need depth, change the tone, not the shadow. Cards step up one cream level. Hover steps up one more. Picking the right step is the answer; 'give it a shadow' is the wrong answer.

dos: Do use British Racing Green (#004225 light, #6FB089 dark text) for action — links, buttons, focus rings, headings
Do use Nugget Ocre (#856814 bronze in light, #C59922 vibrant in dark) for metadata — categories, dates, decorative lines
Do render every a.text-accent as an editorial label: uppercase, 600 weight, 0.08em letter-spacing, 0.875rem
Do keep border-radius: 0 on every native surface — buttons, cards, form controls, tag pills, code blocks, inline code, blockquotes
Do use Conservatory Cream (#F2EFE3) as the body background in light, Forest Floor (#0A1814) — green-tinted, not black — in dark
Do use tonal steps for depth (body → surface → surface-emphasis). Shadows are a state response, not an ambient layer
Do keep Raleway as the sole font family — one typeface across the whole site
Do verify any new color pair against WCAG AA Normal (4.5:1) on the actual rendered substrate — both themes — before adding it to _root.scss
Do document the why of every visual decision inline (the codebase's posture; see docs/THEME.md history for the model)
donts: Don't introduce gradients, glassmorphism, or backdrop-blur effects — the system is matte, flat, and committed
Don't introduce a 'secondary' or 'tertiary' color outside the verde + ocre + cream palette
Don't use pure white (#FFFFFF) on body surfaces — the only legitimate #FFFFFF is text on --eb-brand-solid
Don't use pure black (#000) — use Verde Profundo (#002E19) for the darkest light-mode heading and Forest Floor (#0A1814) for the darkest dark-mode bg
Don't add ambient shadows to cards, modals, or panels — the single hover lift is the whole shadow vocabulary
Don't introduce additional border radii (4px, 8px, 'pill' buttons) — the all-square rule is the spec
Don't add a second font family — no serif 'for editorial', no mono 'for code in prose'

Don't use --bs-accent-lighter as body text on cream in light mode. The token's LIGHT value is #C59922 (vibrant nugget) — only 2.36:1 over cream, fails WCAG. In LIGHT it's reserved for decorative-only use (bg fills, borders, chips). In DARK the same token resolves to #E5C572 and plays a legitimate text role (accent text on solid green panels, e.g. footer CTAs). Mind the asymmetric semantics: the token exists in both themes but the use-case differs. If you need vibrant-ocre as text on cream, you can't — darken to --bs-accent (#856814 bronze) and rely on the Editorial Label treatment for emphasis
Don't render category links as plain <a> text without the Editorial Label treatment — the label is the signature
Don't replicate the AirSpace / Filterworld dev blog template: gradient hero, equal-height card grid, gray sans on white, decorative emoji
Don't replicate the SaaS landing-page cliché: big-number-small-label hero, gradient text on h1, glass cards, icons-in-circles
Don't drift toward Material UI / corporate-dashboard aesthetics: Roboto/Calibri on white, square-card grids of identical height
Don't overcorrect into brutalist anti-design or Y2K revival — the blog is escaping the smooth with craft, not chaos
Don't ship anything that could plausibly be the first one-line-brief output of a code-generation model
Don't edit hex values outside assets/scss/_root.scss — the implementation registry is the executable source of truth
